bank.question: Statement: You are following a cyclist approaching a junction on the left. What should you do — Stay behind them until they have passed the junction.
bank.explanation: You should stay behind until the cyclist has cleared the junction to avoid 'left-hooking' them if they are going straight

bank.question: Statement: Under the 'New Drivers Act', your licence will be revoked if you get how many penalty points — 12 points within 3 years.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: 6 points within 2 years. Under the New Drivers Act, your licence is revoked if you get 6 or more points within 2 years of passing your first practical driving test

bank.question: Statement: You are riding down a long, steep hill. How can you help control your speed — Select a lower gear and use engine braking.
bank.explanation: Engine braking (dropping down gears) helps control your speed without overheating the brakes on long descents

bank.question: Statement: What is meant by the term 'engine braking' — Using the emergency kill switch.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Selecting a lower gear and letting the engine slow the bike. Engine braking is the effect of the engine's compression slowing the bike down when the throttle is closed and a lower gear is selected

bank.question: Statement: What should you do when you see an area of white diagonal stripes bordered by a broken white line on the road — Avoid entering it unless it is necessary and safe to do so.
bank.explanation: White diagonal stripes or chevrons bordered by a broken white line should not be entered unless it is necessary and you can see it is safe

bank.question: Statement: What is known as a 'lifesaver' check in motorcycling — A check of the speedometer before braking.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: A final rearward head check before changing direction. The lifesaver is a final head check into the blind spot before committing to a turn or lane change

bank.question: Statement: If your throttle sticks while riding, what should you do first — Disengage the engine by pulling in the clutch lever.
bank.explanation: If your throttle sticks, you should immediately pull in the clutch to disconnect the engine's power from the rear wheel

bank.question: Statement: What is the primary benefit of wearing a high-visibility waistcoat while riding — It protects you from the wind better.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: It makes you more visible to other road users. High-visibility clothing makes you much easier for other road users to see, especially at junctions where many motorcycle accidents occur

bank.question: Statement: Where would you find red reflective studs on a motorway — Between the edge of the carriageway and the hard shoulder.
bank.explanation: Red studs are placed on the left-hand edge of the motorway to help drivers identify the boundary between the carriage and the hard shoulder

bank.question: Statement: When checking the hydraulic brake fluid level on your motorcycle, what are you looking for — The colour of the fluid only.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: The fluid level is between the maximum and minimum marks. The fluid level should be between the upper and lower marks. If it is low, it could indicate worn pads or a leak

bank.question: Statement: What is the main benefit of wearing a high-visibility gilet over your leather jacket — It makes the rider more visible to other road users.
bank.explanation: A high-visibility gilet or jacket significantly improves the chances of other drivers seeing you, especially in low light

bank.question: Statement: A narrow residential street with cars parked on both sides. A motorcyclist is riding down the center. A ball is visible rolling into the road from between two cars. What should you be most aware of when riding through this narrow residential street — Speed up to get past quickly.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Look for movement or feet between the cars. Parked cars can hide pedestrians, especially children, or car doors might open suddenly. Keep a door's width away where possible

bank.question: Statement: When should you definitely replace your motorcycle helmet — If it has been involved in any impact or crash.
bank.explanation: Modern motorcycle helmets are designed to absorb the energy of an impact once. Even if no damage is visible, the internal structure may be compromised

bank.question: Statement: A triangular warning sign with a red border. The black symbol inside is a zig-zag line that starts by curving to the right and then curves back to the left. What does the sign warn you of — Double bend, first to the left.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Double bend, first to the right. The 'Double Bend' sign warns of a series of bends, the first one being in the direction indicated by the symbol (at the bottom)

bank.question: Statement: How can you improve your visibility to other road users during daylight hours — By wearing bright clothing and using dipped headlights.
bank.explanation: Riding with 'dipped' headlights during the day helps other road users to see you, decreasing the risk of 'looked but failed to see' incidents

bank.question: Statement: A city center street scene showing a motorcycle positioned behind a tram. There are metal rails embedded in the road surface. Why should you take extra care when riding near a tram as shown — The tram will always stop for you.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Trams cannot steer to avoid you. Tram drivers cannot deviate from their tracks. You should give them plenty of room and be particularly careful when crossing the tracks, especially in wet weather

bank.question: Statement: What is the purpose of a side stand cut-out switch — To stop the engine if you try to ride off with the stand down.
bank.explanation: The side stand switch or 'cut-out' is a vital safety feature to prevent riding off with the stand down

bank.question: Statement: You are riding at 30 mph on a dry road. To initiate a turn to the right, what should you do — Pull the handlebars towards you.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Push the handlebar on the side you want to turn towards. Counter-steering requires pushing on the handlebars in the direction you want to turn when travelling at speeds above roughly 10-15 mph

bank.question: Statement: When are you allowed to stop on the hard shoulder of a motorway — In an emergency or breakdown.
bank.explanation: Stopping on the hard shoulder of a motorway is only permitted in an emergency or if told to stop by the police/DVSA

bank.question: Statement: What is the minimum legal tyre tread depth for a motorcycle over 50cc in the UK — 1.6mm.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: 1mm. Tread depth for motorcycles over 50cc must be at least 1mm across three-quarters of the tread pattern

bank.question: Statement: A wide rural single-carriageway road. A motorcyclist is riding in the center of the left-hand lane. The road is clear ahead. What is the safest road position for a motorcyclist in this situation — Stay in the center of your lane.
bank.explanation: When the road is divided by a single broken white line and the lane is wide, stay in the center of your lane to maintain a 'lifesaver' space and visibility

bank.question: Statement: When is fluorescent clothing most effective for a motorcyclist — Only at night under streetlights.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: In daylight and dusk. Fluorescent clothing is most effective during daylight and at dusk to help other road users see you more clearly

bank.question: Statement: When should you be particularly alert for the effects of side winds — When passing high-sided vehicles.
bank.explanation: Crosswinds can significantly affect a motorcycle's stability, especially when passing large vehicles or riding in open areas. High-sided vehicles are particularly vulnerable

bank.question: Statement: How should you dress to stay warm when riding in cold weather — One very thick heavy coat.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Multiple thin layers of clothing. In very cold weather, you should wear several thin layers of clothing to trap warm air and keep your core temperature stable

bank.question: Statement: In the UK, when is it generally considered acceptable to 'filter' through traffic — When traffic is stationary or moving very slowly, with great care.
bank.explanation: Filtering is legal but should be done with extreme caution at low speeds when traffic is stationary or slow

bank.question: Statement: What is the 'two-second rule' used for — Only look at your mirrors every two seconds.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Keep a two-second gap between you and the vehicle in front. The 'two-second rule' helps you maintain a safe separation distance from the vehicle in front in good, dry conditions

bank.question: Statement: What is a specific danger when following a large goods vehicle closely in windy conditions — Turbulence and buffeting from the wind displacement.
bank.explanation: Laminar or smooth airflow behind a large vehicle can cause 'buffeting' or turbulence, which affects the stability of your motorcycle

bank.question: Statement: What is the maximum stopping distance increase you should expect on icy roads — Double the dry distance.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Ten times the dry distance. Stopping distances can be up to ten times longer in icy or snowy conditions due to lack of tyre grip

bank.question: Statement: Why should you ride with dipped headlights during the day — To help other road users see you.
bank.explanation: Dipped headlights help other road users see you more easily, especially in the mirrors of cars, even in bright sunshine

bank.question: Statement: You are about to overtake a cyclist on a road with a 30 mph limit. How much room should you give them — Give them about 30cm of space to stay in your lane.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Give them at least as much room as you would for a car. When overtaking a cyclist, you should give them at least as much room as you would a car (1.5 metres minimum) in case they need to swerve or are blown by wind

bank.question: Statement: Where would you see green reflective studs on a motorway — Between the slip road and the main carriageway.
bank.explanation: Green studs on a motorway are used to mark the edge of the main carriageway where it meets a slip road at an exit or entrance

bank.question: Statement: Where should you NEVER park your motorcycle — In a designated motorcycle bay.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: On a sharp bend. Parking on a sharp bend is dangerous as it forces other road users onto the wrong side of the road at a point where they cannot see oncoming traffic clearly

bank.question: Statement: What is the standard duration for a motorcycle MOT certificate — One year.
bank.explanation: When you take your motorcycle for an MOT, the certificate is usually valid for one year from the date of issue

bank.question: Statement: What is the legal minimum tyre tread depth for a motorcycle over 50cc in the UK — 1.6 mm.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: 1.0 mm. In the UK, the legal minimum tread depth for motorcycle tyres (over 50cc) is 1mm across three-quarters of the tread width

bank.question: Statement: When should you use the right-hand lane of a three-lane motorway — Only when overtaking slower traffic.
bank.explanation: On a three-lane motorway, the right-hand lane is for overtaking only. You must return to the left or middle lane once you have finished

bank.question: Statement: When must you stop your motorcycle after an accident — Only if someone is injured.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: At the scene of the incident. If you are involved in an accident that causes damage or injury, you must stop and provide your details to anyone having reasonable grounds for requiring them

bank.question: Statement: Why can it be dangerous to ride a low-powered motorcycle on a busy motorway — They may struggle to maintain speed or overtake safely in fast-moving traffic.
bank.explanation: Bikes with small engines or low power-to-weight ratios often lack the acceleration needed to merge safely with high-speed motorway traffic

bank.question: Statement: How does carrying a pillion passenger affect the motorcycle's performance — The front of the bike will feel much heavier.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: The stopping distance will be increased. The extra weight of a pillion affects handling and increases the stopping distance; you must leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead

bank.question: Statement: What is a common result of riding with underinflated tyres — The steering will feel heavy and the bike may wander.
bank.explanation: Underinflated tyres have a larger contact patch, increasing friction and making the bike harder to turn and less stable

bank.question: Statement: Which of the following is considered a legal Maneuver for a motorcyclist in the UK — Overtaking on the left on a motorway.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Filtering through slow-moving or stationary traffic. Filtering (or lane splitting) is legal in the UK to bypass slow or stationary traffic, but it must be done safely and at a low speed differential

bank.question: Statement: What should you be particularly aware of when riding in freezing conditions — Watch for 'black ice' in shaded areas or on bridges.
bank.explanation: In very cold weather, ice can form, particularly on bridges and under overhanging trees. You should stay alert for changes in road surface appearance

bank.question: Statement: For a motorcycle over 50cc, what is the minimum legal tyre tread depth — 1.6mm.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: 1mm. The minimum legal tread depth for a motorcycle over 50cc is 1mm across the central three-quarters of the tread

bank.question: Statement: How should your motorcycle be positioned when checking the engine oil level — With the motorcycle held upright on level ground.
bank.explanation: You should always sit on the motorcycle to keep it upright and stable while checking the oil level via a sight glass or dipstick

bank.question: Statement: Where must L-plates be displayed on a motorcycle being ridden by a learner — Only on the rear of the bike.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: On both the front and the rear of the bike. L-plates must be clearly visible from both the front and rear of the motorcycle and must be a legal size (not cut down)

bank.question: Statement: What is the best way to maintain concentration on a long motorcycle journey — Taking regular breaks at least every two hours.
bank.explanation: On a long journey, stopping for regular breaks helps prevent fatigue and keeps your concentration levels high

bank.question: Statement: What is the danger of having a drive chain that is too loose — It will make the exhaust louder.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: It could snap or cause the rear wheel to lock. A loose drive chain can cause poor power delivery, snap, or even lock the rear wheel, leading to a serious accident

bank.question: Statement: What is the legal minimum tread depth for motorcycle tyres (over 50cc) in the UK — 1.0 mm.
bank.explanation: In the UK, the legal minimum tread depth for motorcycles over 50cc is 1mm across three-quarters of the tyre and around the entire circumference

bank.question: Statement: What should you use to top up a battery that is not 'maintenance-free' — Engine oil.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Distilled water. The battery on a motorcycle requires more frequent checks if it's not a 'maintenance-free' type; the electrolyte level should be topped up with distilled water

bank.question: Statement: A narrow country lane with high hedges. Two horses and riders are moving away from the camera on the left-hand side. There is a blind bend ahead. What is the most important precaution to take when passing these road users — Slow down and leave plenty of room when passing.
bank.explanation: Horses are unpredictable and easily spooked; you must pass them slowly and give them a wide berth

bank.question: Statement: What does a diesel spill on the road look like to a motorcyclist — A dry road surface with high grip.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: A very slippery surface, especially when wet. Diesel spills are incredibly slippery for motorcycles and are often found at petrol station exits or roundabouts

bank.question: Statement: What is the primary function of a motorcycle's suspension system — To ensure the tyres stay in contact with the road surface.
bank.explanation: A well-adjusted's suspension ensures the tyres stay in contact with the road, providing better grip and stability

bank.question: Statement: What is the purpose of the solid white line at the side of some roads — To show where parking is allowed.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: To show the edge of the carriageway. Solid white lines at the side of the road are used to mark the edge of the carriageway, helping riders in low visibility

bank.question: Statement: When is it most effective to wear a fluorescent jacket — During daylight hours to improve visibility.
bank.explanation: Fluorescent materials are highly effective during daylight and at dusk, while reflective materials are designed to be seen in the dark under headlights

bank.question: Statement: How often should you take a break when riding on a long journey — Every hour or 50 miles.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: At least every two hours. On a long journey, fatigue can lead to slow reactions and poor judgement; a break every two hours is recommended

bank.question: Statement: What does it mean if you see a flashing red light at a level crossing — Stop and wait behind the stop line.
bank.explanation: A broken red light at a level crossing means you must stop and wait for it to stop flashing before proceeding

bank.question: Statement: You see an emergency vehicle with blue flashing lights behind you. What should you do — Speed up so you don't hold them up.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Pull over and stop as soon as it is safe to do so. Red lights and sirens indicate an emergency vehicle. You must pull over and stop safely as soon as possible to allow them to pass

bank.question: Statement: What is the golden rule for choosing your speed when riding at night — Be able to stop within the distance you can see to be clear.
bank.explanation: At night, your speed should be limited so that you can stop within the distance you can see to be clear with your headlights

bank.question: Statement: Which gas is found in motorcycle exhaust fumes and can be lethal if inhaled in an enclosed space — Carbon dioxide.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Carbon monoxide. Exhaust fumes contain carbon monoxide, which is a colorless, odorless, and highly toxic gas that can be fatal in enclosed spaces

bank.question: Statement: Why is it a disadvantage to wear loose clothing when riding a motorcycle — It can make the motorcycle less stable.
bank.explanation: When travelling at speed, the wind resistance can cause loose clothing to flap, which leads to rider fatigue and can affect the stability of the motorcycle

bank.question: Statement: When driving a car, why can it be difficult to see a motorcyclist at a junction — The rear-view mirror.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: The windscreen pillars. Small motorcycles and mopeds can be easily hidden behind windscreen pillars. Riders should check carefully at junctions

bank.question: Statement: What is the main purpose of performing a 'life-saver' check when riding — To check your blind spots before changing direction.
bank.explanation: Life-saver checks are quick glances over the shoulder to check your blind spots before changing direction or lane

bank.question: Statement: UK warning sign: red triangle with a black silhouette of a bicycle in the middle. What does the sign mean — No cycling allowed.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Cycle route or crossing ahead. A red triangle with a bicycle symbol warns that there is a cycle route or crossing ahead; watch out for cyclists

bank.question: Statement: What is the likely effect of braking hard while you are leaning into a corner — The motorcycle will tend to stand up and go straight on.
bank.explanation: Braking while leaning in a corner can cause the motorcycle to stand up and run wide, potentially into the path of oncoming traffic

bank.question: Statement: When riding through a long, steady bend, where should you primarily be looking — At the front mudguard.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Through the bend to where you want to go. You should always look through the curve to where you want to go; this helps with your balance and line selection

bank.question: Statement: You are following a long vehicle approaching a roundabout. What should you expect — Stay well back and give them plenty of room to manoeuvre.
bank.explanation: Large vehicles need more room to turn and may swing out in the opposite direction before making their turn. Stay back and give them space

bank.question: Statement: When cornering at speeds above 15-20 mph, what technique is used to initiate the lean — Pulling the handlebars towards you.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Applying pressure to the handlebar in the direction you want to go. Counter-steering involves pushing the handlebar in the direction you want to turn when travelling at higher speeds

bank.question: Statement: Which of the following vehicles are most likely to use blue flashing lights — Police and rescue services.
bank.explanation: Blue flashing lights are used by emergency services including police, fire, ambulance, and coastguard

bank.question: Statement: You see a car ahead with bright white lights showing at the rear. What does this usually indicate — The driver is braking hard.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: The vehicle is intending to reverse. Dazzling white lights are usually a sign that a vehicle is reversing. You should stay back and be ready to stop

bank.question: Statement: What is the correct way to check the tension of your drive chain — It should have about 25-30mm of slack.
bank.explanation: A properly adjusted drive chain should have approximately 25-30mm (1 inch) of 'play' or slack at its tightest point

bank.question: Statement: What should you use to top up the fluid level in a conventional lead-acid battery — Engine oil.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Distilled water. A battery may need topping up with distilled water if the fluid level falls below the indicator lines on the casing

bank.question: Statement: Which road users are diamond-shaped traffic signs specifically for — Tram drivers.
bank.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs provide specific instructions or information for tram drivers, though other road users should be aware of them

bank.question: Statement: A view through a motorcycle visor of a straight suburban road during sunset, with a bright orange sun low on the horizon causing significant glare. What specific hazard should you consider when riding in these conditions — You should speed up to get out of the glare quickly.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Be aware that others may not see your signals or lights. Low sun can blind you or other drivers. In this situation, others may not see your signals or brake lights clearly

bank.question: Statement: What should you do if your throttle sticks open while riding — Operate the engine cut-out switch or pull in the clutch.
bank.explanation: If your throttle sticks, the safest immediate action is to pull in the clutch to disconnect the engine from the rear wheel

bank.question: Statement: What should you do if the throttle on your motorcycle becomes stuck open while riding — Change to a higher gear immediately.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Operate the kill switch or pull in the clutch and brake to a stop. If your throttle sticks, you should immediately pull in the clutch to disconnect the engine's power from the rear wheel and then stop safely

bank.question: Statement: What advice should you give a passenger who has never been on a motorcycle before — Keep their feet on the footrests at all times.
bank.explanation: Pillion passengers should lean with the rider and keep their feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped

bank.question: Statement: How will under-inflated tyres affect the handling of your motorcycle — The bike will vibrate at high speeds only.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: The bike will feel heavy and difficult to turn. Under-inflated tyres can cause the bike to 'wander' and feel heavy or unresponsive during cornering

bank.question: Statement: Why should you take extra care when riding over white road markings in wet weather — They can be very slippery when it rains.
bank.explanation: White lines and road markings are often painted with a material that becomes very slippery when wet. Avoid braking or accelerating hard while positioned on them

bank.question: Statement: A loose or damaged exhaust system will primarily increase what — The motorcycle's top speed.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: The noise and pollution levels. A faulty or missing exhaust system can increase noise levels and emit toxic fumes, making the motorcycle illegal and harmful to the environment

bank.question: Statement: How should you ride when moving through a contraflow system on a motorway — Reduce your speed and keep a safe distance],question.
bank.explanation: Contraflow systems involve narrow lanes and temporary barriers; extra caution is needed due to the decreased space

bank.question: Statement: How should you react when you see loose gravel on a bend — Lean the bike further to gain more grip.
bank.explanation: The correct answer is: Slow down and keep the bike upright. Loose gravel significantly reduces tyre grip. You should slow down and keep the bike as upright as possible to avoid low-siding

bank.question: Statement: How can you avoid fatigue when riding a long distance — Plan regular rest stops at least every two hours.
bank.explanation: On long journeys, it is vital to take regular breaks (at least every two hours) to prevent fatigue, which slows reaction times
